clue.text: Settle on style that's specific

parts.note: to settle a debt or doubt is to clear it
a cut is the style of a garment or haircut

explanation.surface: Someone settling on a particular style, choosing one that is precise and specific.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is definite and unambiguous, which is what specific means here.

clue.text: Notice mole below nude's rear

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed below comes second, so it follows the letter from nude's
the rear of a word is its final letter, so take the end of the word nude's

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: An awkward bodily discovery: a mole spotted low on a naked person's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for notice as a verb.

clue.text: Monetary fine is large, around 100 grand essentially

indicators.note: around says the first group of letters encloses the rest

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so take the central letter of grand

explanation.surface: A money penalty so big it is roughly a hundred thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts C plus A (the middle of grand) inside F, IS and L, giving FIS-CA-L.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal relates to public revenue and money, so it is a close synonym of monetary.

clue.text: It's hard to go off mansion I refurbished

indicators.note: a refurbished building is reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A homeowner grumbles that a newly done-up mansion is a hard place to drop off in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' means fall asleep, not explode or turn sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness is the condition in which dropping off to sleep is difficult.

clue.text: Question Spain supporting second African nation, ultimately wanting another one?

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter, and wanting says it is lacking

parts.note: Zambia is a country in southern Africa
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A geography quiz pairing a question about Spain with a second African country.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'African nation' in the wordplay: the answer is another African nation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozambique borders Zambia, so it is another country of Africa as the clue hints.

clue.text: Reluctant to wear extremely cute dress

indicators.note: what is worn goes around, so the outer letters enclose the next piece
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here from cute

parts.note: loth is a variant of loath, meaning unwilling

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to put on a frock that is far too cute.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put garments on them, the verb sense of providing clothing.

clue.text: Getting redness in the face from port

definitions.meaning: blushing or reddening with embarrassment or heat
a harbour town in the Netherlands, also a district of New York

explanation.surface: Coming from a harbour town and turning red in the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddening of the cheeks is the everyday sense, and the Dutch harbour Vlissingen goes by this name in English.

clue.text: Redhead shopping in German stores

indicators.note: a phrase that stores something holds it inside, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A red-haired person out shopping in a German department store.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a common British nickname for a person with red hair.

clue.text: Leo and Don performing improvise musically

indicators.note: performing suggests the two names are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Two musicians called Leo and Don playing on stage and making it up as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: To noodle is to play casual improvised riffs on an instrument.

clue.text: Irish fleeing crime at sea, moving fast

indicators.note: what flees leaves, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: piracy is robbery committed on the high seas

explanation.surface: An Irishman making a quick getaway from a crime on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Pacy is a British word for quick, often said of a fast footballer or a racy story.

clue.text: They feature in ninety per cent of Welsh hymns

definitions.text: They feature in ninety per cent of Welsh hymns

parts.words: They feature in ninety per cent of Welsh hymns
parts.note: the phrase Welsh hymns has ten letters, and nine of them are not vowels

explanation.surface: A statistic about how often something turns up in the hymns of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wales is famous for hymn singing, but the clue is about the letters of the two words: only E is a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters that are not vowels make up nine of the ten letters in the clue's last two words.

clue.text: Forward stroke by son producing untidy handwriting

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
the crawl is the front-facing swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A boy's writing that sprawls messily forward across the page.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is careless, hard-to-read writing.

clue.text: Rare zebra, one Jack found in northern areas around country

indicators.note: rare here means unusual, so the animal's letters are rearranged
found in says the next pair of letters sits inside the reversed group
around says these letters are turned the other way

parts.note: A stands for area, doubled for the plural
I is the Roman numeral for one
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: An unusual zebra and a sailor turning up in the north of some country.
explanation.walkthrough: Areas gives AA, one A per area. 'around' reverses N plus AA, and 'found in' puts I and J inside that reversed group.
explanation.definitionFit: Azerbaijan is a nation in the Caucasus, beside the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Vacuous Etonian and dizzy blonde given peerages

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word Etonian loses its inside and keeps only its ends
dizzy suggests a spin, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An empty-headed public schoolboy and a ditzy blonde both raised to the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian is a pupil of Eton, the elite English school.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made a peer is to be raised to the nobility, the formal sense of the verb.

clue.text: Article, first one that believes in God's existence

definitions.text: one that believes in God's existence

parts.note: the is the definite article
1ST is the short form of first, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A statement of faith: the first article is belief in God.
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in a deity, as opposed to an atheist, holds that a god exists.

clue.text: Trembled, outwardly shocked about French winter strike's conclusion

indicators.note: about says the outer pair of letters goes round the rest
outwardly means on the outside, so keep just the ends of shocked

parts.note: hiver is the French word for winter

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here from strike's

explanation.surface: People shaken by the end of a French winter strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Shook with cold or fear is the plain synonym for trembled.

clue.text: Ship that comes from Newfoundland perhaps, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a Newfoundland is a big dog breed, and the noise from such a dog is a bark

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel arriving from Canada's Atlantic island.
explanation.walkthrough: Newfoundland looks like the Canadian island, but here it is the large breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A barque is a sailing vessel with three or more masts.

clue.text: Model almost relaxed for a change hosting politician

indicators.note: a host takes in a guest, so the shuffled letters hold the next piece
for a change says the letters are rearranged
almost says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A model who is nearly relaxed welcomes a politician for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims relaxed to RELAXE, 'for a change' shuffles it to EXELAR, and 'hosting' puts MP inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is an ideal example to be copied, as a model is.

clue.text: Old man stops others getting meal

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so this piece goes inside the next

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
old man is slang for father, which is pa

explanation.surface: A father blocks the others from getting their dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal or feast.

clue.text: Kids with beer staggering, reaching pavement edge

indicators.note: staggering means lurching unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drunken youngsters weaving along until they reach the edge of the footpath.
explanation.walkthrough: The kerb is the British name for the curb, the raised edge of the pavement (sidewalk).
explanation.definitionFit: The side of the road by the curb is where the footpath meets the street.

clue.text: Discovered Kent student is tempted initially to join armed forces

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover removed, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: L is for learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of tempted

explanation.surface: A student from Kent is tempted to sign up for the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service.

clue.text: Exam everyone gets hold of the day before!

indicators.note: something that gets hold of another holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: all means everyone
eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Every student grabs their notes on the evening before a big test.
explanation.walkthrough: A level is the advanced school-leaving exam in England and Wales, taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: The advanced-level school-leaving test, sat in British schools before university.

clue.text: On holiday touring US city, at all events

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: away means gone on holiday
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Tourists on vacation going round an American city, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway and at all events both mean in any case, regardless.

clue.text: Ignorance evident in elderly care till in-laws retired

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
what is evident in some words can be seen inside them, so the letters sit within this stretch

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being unable to read shows when in-laws who have retired move into care.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Ignorance evident' as the definition and left the hidden word with no signal; 'evident in' is that signal, so the definition is 'Ignorance' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiteracy is lack of learning, especially inability to read, a form of ignorance.

clue.text: Facing pet with no energy, the two of us cried

indicators.note: facing means put in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: two people speaking of themselves say we

indicators.note: with no says the letter is removed

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A couple tearfully facing a pet that has lost all its energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed tears is the plain synonym for cried.

clue.text: Fascination over Dick Grayson's relationship to Bruce Wayne?

definitions.text: Dick Grayson's relationship to Bruce Wayne?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a draw is an attraction or pull, a fascination

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the bond between Robin and Batman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the comics Dick Grayson, the first Robin, is the young charge of Bruce Wayne, alias Batman.
explanation.definitionFit: Grayson is a minor placed in Wayne's legal guardianship, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Miss flight

definitions.meaning: to avoid or elude, as a detail slips past one's notice
a getaway or breaking free from captivity

explanation.definitionFit: A name may elude one's memory, and a prisoner's breakout is a getaway: both senses fit.

clue.text: Cutting wood, was Barney regularly finding time for a cuppa?

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so the picked letters go within the wood

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A man called Barney chopping timber pauses to make a pot of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause at work for a cup of tea, the British workplace ritual.
